gaps.construct: inst.update(msg) where inst is either an OpenSSL HMAC object or a hashlib hash object
gaps.description: There is no interface, trait or method declaration, so 'anything with update' cannot be declared. Hasher is used as if it were one.

gaps.construct: self._hmac or self._inner (truthiness-based fallback over None)
gaps.description: There is no truthiness and no 'first present of' expression. It needs a nested choose, so a two-line method becomes nine body lines.

gaps.construct: AttributeError raised implicitly when both are None
gaps.description: The implicit crash must become an explicit named failure in the header. That is better, but it adds a failure the original never declares.

gaps.construct: mutating a hasher held inside a maybe field of an editable record
gaps.description: The doc does not say whether `when some h` binds by reference, which an in-place update needs, or by copy.

gaps.construct: msg may be any bytes-like object (buffer protocol)
gaps.description: Only Bytes exists, and there is no buffer protocol or view type.

invented_syntax: Hasher as an interface-like type with an update operation
update_hasher h with msg called on a value bound by choose, expecting in-place mutation
notes: This is the smallest function in the batch, but it hits the same wall as F38: Scribe cannot say 'one of several implementations of the same operation', which is a pervasive need in library code. A `first some of a, b` expression, or `or else` (already used in `together`) applied to maybe values, would remove the nested choose.
